newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar court rejects delay in president vote.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar court rejects delay in president vote.

text.p: A Madagascar court rejected on Tuesday a government request to delay a second run-off presidential election and said it must take place on or before January 3.

Boto Victor, president of the High Consitutional Court, said it rejected an application from the government for the second round to be postponed more than the 31 days after the announcement of official results as set by the constitution.
The government had requested the delay, arguing the New Year holidays would interfere with the run-off and the cost of organising the second round had to be approved in the 1997 budget.
Former military leader Didier Ratsiraka and former president Albert Zafy will contest the second round run-off election.
Official results of the first round of voting on November 3 issued on Monday showed Ratsiraka took 36.61 percent against 23.39 percent for Zafy.
Victor reported numerous anomalies in the first round of voting but said they did not change the overall results.
The election was called after Zafy, 69, who was elected president in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority. The HCC upheld the impeachment.

The strength of support for Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, has surprised many observers. He was reviled by many people in the early 1990s for using the army to resist the pro-democracy movement on the vast island with a population of 14 million, most of whom live in chronic poverty.

The HCC said millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo took 15.13 percent of the first round vote followed by interim president Norbert Ratsirahonana with 10.14 percent. Parliament Speaker Richard Andriamanjato took 4.94 percent. Ten other candidates took between two and 0.37 percent.
